text:
ops-lead: Heads up — planning a maintenance window for thermal-margin adjustments + NIC microcode on az3 GPUs. Target: Sat 02:00 UTC, 3hr slot. We'll cordon/drain racks in 10-min cohorts to avoid surge.

jordan: ETA on expected throughput loss? will hosted API see 5xx or just latency bump?

ops-lead: main impact = slight latency tail for a few cohorts during drain. No planned 5xx. We'll keep two small canaries in each region to verify before continuing.

sree: can we avoid draining high-priority dedicated pools? several tenants in az3 have reserved capacity.

ops-lead: yes — dedicated pools (ded-*) will be pinned. We'll only touch shared/interruptible pools and a small set of overflow nodes.

matt_b: can we run a quick capacity check now — how many idle GPUs in us-east/shared? if < 15% we might need to defer.

ivan: ran a quick query: shared idle ~18% across us-east1, eu-west1 combined. apac-west1 is tight (8%). Suggest we keep APAC cohorts to the end and enable burst-backfill from us-east.

ops-lead: good call. Plan update: start with eu/us cohorts, leave apac for last and only proceed if backfill can cover 20% request spike.

nora: oncall, can you confirm cross-region bandwidth for KV-cache seeding? warmup might cause short egress spikes. @oncall-bot please run prep check.

oncall-bot: preflight checks kicked off: netpath test -> OK; kv-seed bandwidth estimate ~120MB/s for full cohort, will throttle to 40MB/s.

jordan: agree with throttling. Also suggest prewarming prefix cache before draining to reduce token regen cost.

ops-lead: we'll run a prewarm job 30m before each cohort drains. Command (example):

```bash
./maintenance/drain-cohort.sh --cohort az3-rack-11 --prewarm-prefixes /opt/prewarm/list.txt --kv-throttle 40mBps
```

matt_b: cost question — what's expected extra egress/backfill spend? rough ballpark?

ops-lead: estimate = ~ $1.2k for the 3hr window (egress + temporary burst infra). I'll add to the weekly ops budget.

ivan: can we avoid running any large evals or batch jobs during that window? I'll send a cancel message to data-team.

ops-lead: yes pls cancel scheduled batch runs in az3 between 01:30-05:00 UTC. nora, can you handle customer comms for any tenants likely to see tail-latency?

nora: will draft short note to customers with reserved pools + status page blurb.

jordan: I'll be on standby for canary verification. If top-of-queue latency >= 1200ms for 5 consecutive minutes, we rollback per the runbook.

ops-lead: perfect. Rollback trigger noted. Final checklist: prewarm jobs scheduled, canaries isolated, dedicated pools pinned, apac last. If no objections, we'll file the maintenance ticket and schedule the window. :thumbsup:

matt_b: +1

ivan: +1

sree: +1

ops-lead: ok filing ticket now -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2199 :alarm_clock:
